title.en: Gopu, Simmi and Raj on the way to school

text.en: Gopu, Simmi and Raj walk to school every day. On the way they see flowers, mountains and streams, and so many kinds of plants. Today we get to know the families of plants and the parts of a plant.

The three friends notice that plants come in so many sizes and shapes: tiny, small, large and bushy, thin and curvy, straight and tall. Some leaves are rough and some are smooth, and the friends love to touch and smell them. Raj loves the jamun tree with its thick, shiny leaves, tiny white flowers and little green fruits that turn red and then purple. Plants can be put into groups: trees, shrubs, herbs, grasses, climbers and creepers.
A tree has a big trunk of wood and many branches that spread out with leaves. Its roots go deep down into the soil. Mango, coconut, khejri, jackfruit, banyan, amaltas, peepal and chinar are all trees. We can write the names of trees we have seen near our home or on the way to school.
Not all plants grow tall like trees. A shrub is a medium-sized plant with several woody stems and branches growing close to the ground. Hibiscus, rose, tulsi and curry leaf are shrubs, and tulsi at home is a shrub too. Toor, masoor, moong and urad dal are all seeds of shrubs.
Herbs are smaller plants with soft, green stems that do not become woody. Mint, tomato, coriander and mustard are herbs. Grasses are a kind of herb. Their leaves are long, thin and flat and their stems are hollow. The grains we eat, like paddy, wheat, bajra, jowar and ragi, are seeds of large grasses. Sugarcane and bamboo are tall grasses, and bamboo is special because it stays alive for longer than a year.
A money plant has a long, thin stem and cannot stand up by itself. If it finds something to climb on, it goes up the wall or the tree, and then it is a climber. If it finds nothing to climb, it creeps and spreads on the ground, and then it is a creeper. Jasmine and bottle gourd are climbers, while watermelon and pumpkin are creepers. Some climbers even take their food from the plant on which they climb, and some plants behave like climbers or creepers depending on the support they get.
We can choose one plant, such as a shrub with a thick stem or a tree, and make friends with it. We name it like a pet, water it every day, and protect it. We observe its leaves, flowers and fruits, and note how many, what colour and what shape. We keep a record of the date, the month and the weather, and visit as often as we can. We notice new leaves growing, old brown leaves falling, and flowers and fruit appearing.
Leaves of different plants have different colours, shapes and sizes, like peepal, mango, lotus and khejri. Leaves smell different too: tulsi, coriander, curry leaf, mint and lemon grass all have lovely different smells. Raj's brother cannot see, but he can smell fruits like mango, pineapple, jackfruit, guava and jamun from far away. The main parts of a plant are the root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit and seed, and we can see them all in a tomato plant.
Bark is the hard outer covering of a tree trunk, and we can look and touch to see animals, insects and plants on it. We can press paper on the bark and rub a crayon on it to get a bark pattern. Sugar is made from the stem of the sugarcane, and bamboo is the tallest grass. Rafflesia, found in Mizoram, is the biggest flower and is as big as an umbrella.

problem.en: Which group is a tulsi plant, and why?

text.en: Look at the stems: tulsi has several woody stems close to the ground.
It is not tall with one big trunk.
So tulsi is a shrub.

why.en: Medium size and woody stems make it a shrub.

problem.en: Is a money plant a climber or a creeper?

text.en: It has a long thin stem that cannot stand by itself.

why.en: Climbers and creepers have thin, flexible stems.

text.en: If it climbs a wall or tree, it is a climber.
If it spreads on the ground, it is a creeper.
So it can be either, depending on the support.

why.en: The textbook note says some plants act as both.

problem.en: Sort into tree, shrub, herb, grass, climber or creeper: mint, banyan, rose, wheat, jasmine, pumpkin.

text.en: Mint has a soft, green stem, so it is a herb.
Banyan has a big trunk, so it is a tree.
Rose has woody stems close to the ground, so it is a shrub.
Wheat has thin flat leaves and hollow stems, so it is a grass.
Jasmine climbs for support, so it is a climber.
Pumpkin spreads on the ground, so it is a creeper.

prompt.en: Tell a friend the six kinds of plants and the parts of a plant.

requiredIdeas.en: Trees have a big wooden trunk, shrubs have several woody stems, herbs have soft stems
Grasses have thin flat leaves and hollow stems; grains are seeds of grasses
Climbers climb for support and creepers spread along the ground
A plant has root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit and seed

commonMisconceptions.en: Dal and grains are not seeds
A climber and a creeper are exactly the same

points.en: Plants are of many kinds: trees, shrubs, herbs, grasses, climbers and creepers.
Trees have a big trunk, shrubs have several woody stems, and herbs have soft stems.
Grains are seeds of large grasses, and dals are seeds of shrubs.
Climbers climb for support and creepers spread along the ground.
A plant has root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit and seed, and leaves differ in colour, shape, size and smell.
